title: DNA and Protein Synthesis
seo_title: DNA and Protein Synthesis Worksheets: Transcription and Translation (Biology)
standard_text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the structure of DNA determines the structure of proteins which carry out the essential functions of life through systems of specialized cells.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on DNA and protein synthesis (NGSS HS-LS1-1): base pairing, transcription, codon tables, translation and mutations. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Three bases make a codon; the order of amino acids sets the protein's shape and job.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA → mRNA → protein. The order of bases in a gene sets the order of amino acids, and that order sets the protein's shape and job.

  • Pairing: DNA A–T, G–C. RNA uses U: A–U.
  • Transcription (nucleus): DNA template → mRNA.
  • Translation (ribosome): every 3 bases (a codon) → 1 amino acid. AUG starts; UAA, UAG, UGA stop.
Example

DNA template TAC GGA → mRNA?

T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C

Answer: AUG CCU

Example

mRNA with 60 coding bases → how many amino acids?

3 bases per amino acid

60 ÷ 3

Answer: 20

Common mistakes

  • Pairing A with U in DNA. DNA uses T.
  • Keeping T in mRNA. RNA uses U.
  • Reading one base as one amino acid. A codon is 3 bases.
  • Thinking translation happens in the nucleus. It happens at ribosomes.

faq.q: What is the difference between transcription and translation?
faq.a: Transcription copies a gene into mRNA in the nucleus. Translation reads the mRNA at a ribosome to build a protein.

faq.q: How do you use a codon table?
faq.a: Split the mRNA into groups of three bases from the start codon AUG, then look up each codon's amino acid until a stop codon.

faq.q: How can one base change matter?
faq.a: It can change one amino acid (substitution), stop the protein early (nonsense) or shift every codon after it (insertion or deletion).

items.q: Why do proteins with different amino acid orders do different jobs?
c: Amino acid order has no effect.
All proteins have the same shape.
The order determines how the protein folds into its shape.
items.e: Shape determines function.

items.q: Name a protein job in the body.
items.e: Proteins carry out life functions.

items.q: Sofia removes one base near the start of a gene. Why is this usually harmful?
c: It changes only the last amino acid.
It only changes the DNA color.
It shifts the reading frame and changes the protein's shape.
items.e: A frameshift scrambles every codon after it.

items.q: A mutation turns a codon into a stop codon. What is it called?
items.e: The protein is cut short.

One base changes: AUG UUU CAU becomes AUG UCU CAU. What happens to the protein?
c: One amino acid changes: Phe becomes Ser.
Every amino acid after the change is different.
The protein gets one amino acid longer.
items.e: A substitution changes only one codon: UUU → UCU.

items.q: Which mutation usually changes a protein the most?
c: deleting three bases in a row at the end
changing one base near the end
deleting one base near the start of the gene
items.e: An early frameshift changes almost every codon.

items.q: Zoe adds one base to the middle of a gene. What is the most likely effect?
c: The reading frame shifts, so many amino acids after it change.
The gene gets one extra amino acid only.
items.e: Insertions and deletions cause frameshifts.
